title: OpenAI首款AI硬件，为什么是个没有屏幕的「甜甜圈」
content: OpenAI and Jony Ive's design studio LoveFrom are developing a screenless, hockey-puck-sized ring-shaped AI device priced at $300–400, expected next year. The battery-powered device features speakers, microphones, lights, cameras, and environmental sensors, with movable mechanical components that respond during interactions. Positioned as an "AI-first computer," it aims to replace screen-based interaction with ambient voice and visual awareness, understanding user context through continuous environmental sensing. This represents OpenAI's bid to create AI-native hardware that eliminates traditional app and touchscreen dependency, while avoiding the privacy concerns of wearable devices like smart glasses.

title: Enforcing data residency with single-Region Claude Code on Amazon Bedrock
content: To enforce single-Region data residency for Claude Code on Amazon Bedrock, choose between two paths based on your AWS Region. Use Mantle (Path 1) in seven supported Regions including Ireland and Tokyo, where native single-Region routing requires only environment variables. For London (eu-west-2), use classic Amazon Bedrock (Path 2) with application inference profiles since Mantle lacks in-Region support there. Both paths require an IAM policy with aws:RequestedRegion conditions to block cross-Region calls. Verify compliance via CloudTrail: check InvokeModel events for classic Bedrock or CreateInference data events for Mantle, ensuring all events occur only in your target Region.

title: Agent Skills for Automated Reasoning policies in Amazon Bedrock
content: Amazon Bedrock Automated Reasoning checks validate AI outputs using formal logic rather than statistical sampling, providing mathematical certainty of compliance. AWS offers six open-format Agent Skills—builder, reviewer, tester, debugger, deployer, and validator—that enable coding agents to manage the full policy lifecycle in code. Each skill contains instructions, reference materials, and runnable Python scripts calling Bedrock APIs. The skills install into any compatible agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Kiro). Key lessons include: verdicts are explainable with supporting or contradicting rules; "SATISFIABLE" differs from "VALID" (consistency versus entailment); and build slots are automatically managed during refinement.
